intent: Make production builds leave both empty and populated SQLite data directories unchanged. Move any required Hermes model and credential import to an explicit post-backup seed path, and keep fresh-install and update fixtures representative of that order.
programme: Prerequisite T-0161 under the operator's tooling-13 ruling and the 2026-09-26 plan. It follows the T-0157 framework security update. No structural cleanup is authorised by this batch.
invariants: A production build leaves a fresh isolated data directory empty and does not change bytes or modes of an existing SQLite database or its sidecars.
Runtime first boot still creates and migrates a database; build-only suppression cannot persist into next start, dev or request workers.
Hermes models and credentials previously imported during prebuild remain available through an explicit import step after a backup, and failures cannot report success silently.

Setup and in-app update back up before migration or import, retain Windows development and preserve test identities. The install harness uses an explicit seed fixture rather than a prebuild side effect.
rollback: Revert the build lifecycle, import step and install fixture together, restore the prior manifest and repeat the complete gate in an isolated checkout. A rollback restores pre-backup database writes; block setup/update on a live data directory until the ordering hazard is fixed again.
notes: Observed 2026-09-26 in isolated validation checkout after T-0157: npx next build with a fresh PS_DATA_DIR and no npm prebuild exited 0 but created patterstage.db, -wal and -shm; the database reached schema_version 42. package.json prebuild separately calls prebuild-db.mjs, which opens repository data, may unlink an old DB and seeds. The build risk therefore has two causes. Both scripts/lib/ps-migrate.sh and scripts/tooling/ps-deploy.mjs continue after backup failure, so a failure path is in this batch's claim. Hosted T-0157 push/PR CI and both Gitleaks workflows all completed success at 8d336c4d before implementation. EOS taskops.route_record ruled R2 from declared migrates-schema; taskops.create_task cannot validate this venture because kernel/schemas/task-record.schema.json is absent here and the sibling EOS schema rejects PatterStage's established custom task fields. Record creation uses the routed result and the existing venture record shape; the task-writing gap remains an open foundations defect, not a passing schema check.
